1.title: Google Cloud Security Products, AI Security and Trust
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Google Cloud Security Products, A I Security and Trust. It covers the exam area five. Trust and security with Google Cloud. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. five point two Describe the business value of making Google part of an organization's security team: how Google Cloud secures every layer of the A I stack. Google Threat Intelligence. Security Command Center. Google Security Operations. Google's secure-by-design platform. A I-assisted and A I-focused security offerings (Gemini in Google Security Operations, A I Protection, Model Armor). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five. Trust and security with Google Cloud (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Secure by design
1.text: Secure by design. The figure shows this: Google's defense in depth: layers from hardware and network to data, identity and operations.

1.title: Secure by design, continued
1.text: Secure by design. Google Cloud uses a defense-in-depth, multilayered approach, so Google acts as part of your security team. Core infrastructure. Own data centers, purpose-built servers and networking, custom security hardware and software. Network. Google's global private network and D dos (distributed denial of service) protection. Platform and services. Encryption by default and security built into products. Identity and access. I A M, two-step verification. Operations. Threat intelligence and security operations at Google scale. The A I stack has layers too: infrastructure, data, models, platform and agents. Google Cloud secures every layer, so organizations can use A I safely. Exam tip: Secure by design means security starts in the hardware and software Google builds itself, not as an add-on.

1.title: Google Threat Intelligence
1.text: Google Threat Intelligence. Purpose. Proactive insight into who is targeting you and how, so you can set defenses and respond. Sources. Google's vast global visibility, Mandiant's frontline incident response expertise, Virus Total's crowdsourced threat detection. Result. A unified verdict and context about threats; Gemini helps surface the threats that matter to you.

1.title: Security Command Center (SCC)
1.text: Security Command Center (S C C). Security Command Center discovers, prioritizes and remediates security risks and misconfigurations across the Google Cloud environment. Posture management. Finds misconfigurations and vulnerabilities without agents. Threat detection. Detects active threats in near real time. A I protection. Finds A I assets, prioritizes risk, secures models and agents. Virtual red teaming. Simulates attackers to find attack paths. Compliance Manager. Tracks compliance and evidence. Data security posture management. Finds and monitors sensitive data.

1.title: Google Security Operations and AI security
1.text: Google Security Operations and A I security. Google Security Operations. Unified security operations platform: collects telemetry at scale and speeds detection, investigation and response (sim and soar). Gemini in Google Security Operations. A I assistant that summarizes threats, helps investigate and writes queries. A I Protection. Discover, assess and protect A I workloads (within Security Command Center). Model Armor. Screens prompts and responses of A I models for prompt injection, sensitive data leakage and harmful content. Exam tip: Model Armor protects A I conversations. Security Command Center finds and prioritizes risk. Google Security Operations detects and responds.

1.title: Other security offerings
1.text: Other security offerings. Cloud V P C. Private, isolated virtual network. Cloud V P N (virtual private network). Encrypted tunnel over the internet to your network. Cloud Interconnect. Dedicated or partner private connection to your network. Firewalls. Rules that allow or block traffic. Cloud Armor. Protects applications from D dos and web attacks. Cloud Logging. Collects logs for auditing and investigation. I A M. Who can do what on which resource.

1.title: Other security offerings, continued
1.text: Other security offerings. Sensitive Data Protection. Discover, classify and de-identify sensitive data (formerly Cloud Data Loss Prevention). Confidential Computing. Encrypts data while it is in use inside the processor. Certificate Manager. Manages T L S certificates for secure connections. Identity-Aware Proxy (I A P). Application-level access by user identity and context, without a V P N.

1.title: Trust, residency and compliance
1.text: Trust, residency and compliance. Transparency reports. Google publishes how it handles government requests for data. Third-party audits. Independent auditors verify controls against recognized standards. Data residency. Where data is stored; customers can choose regions. Digital sovereignty. Control over data, operations and access under local law. Compliance resource center. Reports and certifications that help meet industry and regional compliance. Exam tip: Trust comes from transparency and independent proof: transparency reports and third-party audits. Residency equals where the data sits.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company wants to know which threat actors target its industry, using insight from Google, Mandiant and Virus Total. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Google Threat Intelligence. Google Threat Intelligence combines Google's visibility, Mandiant's expertise and Virus Total's database.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A security team wants to find misconfigurations and vulnerabilities across its Google Cloud environment and rank the risks. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Security Command Center. Security Command Center discovers, prioritizes and remediates risks and misconfigurations.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company runs a chatbot and wants to block prompt injection and prevent sensitive data from leaking in answers. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Model Armor, which screens prompts and responses. Model Armor protects A I prompts and responses against prompt injection, leakage and harmful content.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants one platform to ingest telemetry, detect threats and speed up response, with A I help. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Google Security Operations, with Gemini. Google Security Operations is the unified security operations platform, with Gemini to assist analysts.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company wants to protect data while it is being processed in memory. Which technology fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Confidential Computing, which encrypts data in use. Confidential Computing encrypts data in use in the processor.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A customer must keep its data in a specific country to meet local rules. Which concept applies? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Data residency, the location where data is stored. Data residency is the choice of where data is stored, which Google Cloud lets customers control.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are the three sources of Google Threat Intelligence? Answer: Google's visibility, Mandiant and Virus Total. Question two. What does Model Armor protect? Answer: A I prompts and responses. Question three. What does Cloud Armor protect against? Answer: D dos and web attacks.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does Identity-Aware Proxy do? Answer: Gives application access by identity and context, without a V P N. Question five. What does Confidential Computing protect? Answer: Data in use. Question six. How does Google show trust? Answer: Transparency reports and third-party audits.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Secure by design: own data centers, purpose-built hardware, layers across the A I stack. Threat intelligence: Google, Mandiant, Virus Total; unified verdict. S C C: posture, threat detection, A I protection, red teaming, compliance. sec ops and A I: Google Security Operations, Gemini, A I Protection, Model Armor. Others: V P C, V P N, Interconnect, Cloud Armor, Logging, I A M, Sensitive Data Protection, Confidential Computing, Certificate Manager, I A P. Trust: transparency reports, audits, residency, sovereignty, compliance resources.
